subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on network topologies and protocols, then mark my answer against the OCR spec.
promptWeak: Explain network topologies and protocols for GCSE OCR Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a LAN?
options: A network that only connects wireless devices together
A network covering a small geographical area, usually on a single site with hardware owned by the organisation
A global network of interconnected networks
A network covering a large geographical area, often using infrastructure hired from third parties
questions.explain: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small geographical area (e.g. one site/building) and the organisation typically owns the hardware and infrastructure. A WAN covers a large area and usually leases infrastructure from a third party.

questions.q: A company links its offices in London and Manchester so they act as one network. What type of network connection is this?
options: A star topology
A PAN
A WAN
A LAN
questions.explain: Connecting sites over a large geographical distance (London to Manchester) forms a WAN (Wide Area Network). WANs commonly use infrastructure hired from a telecommunications provider.

questions.q: Which of these is a factor that affects the performance of a network?
options: The size of the monitor connected
The bandwidth available
The brand of the operating system
The colour of the network cables
questions.explain: Bandwidth (the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted per second) directly affects performance. Other J277 factors include the number of users, transmission media, and interference/error rate.

questions.q: A school network becomes very slow at break time when hundreds of students connect at once. Which factor best explains this?
options: Too many users sharing the available bandwidth
The router has run out of MAC addresses
The IP addresses have expired
The DNS server has been switched off
questions.explain: When many users share the same bandwidth simultaneously, each user gets a smaller share and the network becomes congested, reducing performance. The number of connected devices/users is a key J277 performance factor.

questions.q: In a client-server network, what is the main role of the server?
options: To replace the need for any network hardware
To provide and manage centralised resources and services for the clients
To act as an equal to every other computer with no central control
To store data only on individual client machines
questions.explain: In a client-server model, the server provides centralised control, storage, security and shared services (e.g. files, email), and clients request these services from it.

questions.q: Two home users connect their laptops directly to share files, with no central computer controlling access. Which model is this?
options: Star topology only
Client-server
Peer-to-peer
Mesh backbone
questions.explain: In a peer-to-peer network all computers are equal, sharing resources directly with each other with no central server. It is cheap and simple but harder to back up and secure centrally.

questions.q: In a star topology, how are the devices connected?
options: Every device is connected to every other device directly
Devices are connected in a single closed loop
Each device is connected to a central switch or hub
Devices are connected one after another in a line
questions.explain: In a star topology every node connects to a central device (usually a switch). Data goes via the central device to its destination, which improves security and reliability of individual links.

questions.q: What is an advantage of a star topology compared with other layouts?
options: It uses the least possible amount of cable in every case
If one cable fails, only that one device is affected, not the whole network
It requires no central device at all
A single cable break disconnects every device
questions.explain: Because each device has its own dedicated link to the central switch, a single cable failure only disconnects that one device. A drawback is that if the central switch fails, the whole network goes down.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a full mesh topology?
options: All devices connect to one central hub
Only two devices can ever be connected
Devices are arranged in a single ring
Every device is connected directly to every other device
questions.explain: In a full mesh topology every device is directly connected to every other device, giving multiple paths for data. This provides high reliability because data can be re-routed if a link fails.

questions.q: Why is a mesh topology well suited to critical systems such as the internet backbone?
options: It is the cheapest topology to cable
It stops any device from ever being added
It has no single point of failure, so data can be re-routed around broken links
It requires only one cable in total
questions.explain: A mesh has many redundant connections, so if one link fails data is re-routed via another path. This resilience makes it ideal where reliability is critical, though it needs a lot of cabling/connections.

questions.q: Which is generally an advantage of a wired (e.g. fibre/Ethernet) connection over wireless?
options: It never needs any cabling
It offers greater mobility for the user
It typically offers faster and more reliable data transfer with less interference
It always covers a larger area than any Wi-Fi
questions.explain: Wired connections are typically faster, more reliable and more secure, with less interference. Wireless offers mobility and easier setup but is more prone to interference and signal weakening over distance.

questions.q: Which piece of hardware creates a wireless network by letting Wi-Fi devices connect to a wired network?
options: A network switch only
A domain name server
A Wireless Access Point (WAP)
A trace table
questions.explain: A Wireless Access Point (WAP) allows Wi-Fi enabled devices to connect wirelessly and links them to the wired network. A switch alone only connects wired devices within a LAN.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of encrypting data sent across a network?
options: To compress the data to a smaller size
To make the data transmit faster
To scramble the data so it cannot be understood if intercepted
To convert the data into a domain name
questions.explain: Encryption scrambles data using a key so that only the intended recipient (with the key) can read it. If intercepted, the ciphertext is meaningless. It protects confidentiality, not speed or size.

questions.q: Which statement about MAC addresses is correct?
options: A MAC address changes every time a device joins a new network
A MAC address is the same as a domain name
A MAC address is a unique physical address assigned to a network interface, normally permanent
A MAC address is allocated by the DNS server
questions.explain: A MAC address is a unique hardware (physical) address assigned to a NIC by the manufacturer and is normally fixed. An IP address, by contrast, is assigned to a device on a network and can change.

questions.q: Which network device uses IP addresses to forward data between different networks?
options: A NIC
A WAP
A switch
A router
questions.explain: A router uses IP addresses to route data packets between different networks (e.g. from a LAN to the internet). A switch uses MAC addresses to direct traffic within a single LAN.

questions.q: Why are agreed network standards important?
options: They remove the need for any protocols
They make all networks run at exactly the same speed
They stop new devices being added to a network
They ensure hardware and software from different manufacturers can communicate together
questions.explain: Standards are agreed rules that allow devices and software from different manufacturers to work together (interoperability). Without common standards, equipment from different vendors could not reliably communicate.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to securely transfer web pages between a web server and a browser?
options: FTP
SMTP
IMAP
HTTPS
questions.explain: HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) transfers web pages with encryption for security. Plain HTTP does the same but without encryption. FTP transfers files, and SMTP/IMAP relate to email.

questions.q: Which pair of protocols is used to retrieve/receive emails from a mail server?
options: HTTP and HTTPS
SMTP and DNS
FTP and TCP
POP and IMAP
questions.explain: POP and IMAP are used to retrieve emails from a mail server (IMAP keeps mail on the server; POP typically downloads and removes it). SMTP is used to send emails.

questions.q: The TCP/IP model used at GCSE has how many layers?
options: 5 layers
7 layers
4 layers
3 layers
questions.explain: The TCP/IP model has 4 layers: Application, Transport, Internet (Network), and Link (Network Access). The 7-layer model is the OSI model, which is not required for J277.

questions.q: In the 4-layer TCP/IP model, which layer is where protocols such as HTTP, FTP and SMTP operate?
options: The Transport layer
The Application layer
The Internet layer
The Link layer
questions.explain: Application-facing protocols like HTTP, FTP and SMTP work at the Application layer. The Transport layer (e.g. TCP) manages the connection, the Internet layer handles addressing/routing (IP), and the Link layer deals with physical hardware.
